mods.name: BuildFromChests
mods.description:
Building with the hammer uses materials from chests near you, not just your inventory.

How it works
- Pieces you place take materials from your inventory first, then from chests within range (default 20 m).
- The build menu shows how many of each material you have in total, so you can see what is possible before you place anything.
- Works together with CraftFromChests; each can be turned off on its own.

Settings: range and whether the counts show.
mods.notes: Faster: the build menu's chest checks are worked out once and reused instead of for every piece. The build menu shows how many of each material you have (inventory plus chests).

mods.name: BuildOrders
mods.description:
Plan pieces as shared ghost build orders for everyone in your party.

How it works
- Hold Left Alt and place with the hammer to plan a piece instead of building it. It shows as a see-through ghost that other players see too.
- Your own placement snaps onto a ghost, and the ghost disappears once the real piece is built.
- G selects the piece you are looking at to build more like it, and Delete removes a ghost. F9 shows or hides all ghosts.
- A panel totals the materials your orders still need.

Settings: ghost opacity, view distance, snap distance and the keys.
mods.notes: Smoother: finished orders are found with a quick nearby check instead of scanning every piece in the world, ghosts appear a few at a time (closest first), removed ghosts free their memory, and clearing a cluster saves once. Ghosts are see-through (GhostOpacity).

mods.name: CraftFromChests
mods.description:
Crafting stations, and hand-crafting from your inventory, use materials from nearby chests.

How it works
- Anything you can reach within the range counts toward a recipe. The game takes the materials from your inventory first, then from the chests.
- The crafting menu shows how many of each material you have in total.
- A Chest lines button beside the crafting tabs draws lines from the station to every chest in use; a Range button cycles the distance (5 to 30 m).

Settings: range (default 20 m), whether counts and lines show, and the position and size of the buttons.
mods.notes: Smoother: the crafting-screen buttons are only looked after while the inventory is open and aren't repositioned every frame, and the chest checks are worked out once and reused (no more stutter when opening the inventory). Hand-crafting from the inventory uses nearby chests, and the crafting window shows how many of each material you have.

mods.name: FeedFromChests
mods.description:
Smelters, kilns, cooking racks, fires and fermenters can use items from nearby chests.

How it works
- Press E at a station: it adds from a chest if you have none, or opens a menu if there is a choice. Look at a station and press F to always get the menu of everything you can add.
- The menu lists items from the lesser to the greater (wood, fine wood, core wood...) and has a Fill option that tops the station up.
- Nothing is created from nothing: every item comes out of your inventory or a chest.

Settings: range (default 15 m), automatic adding, always open the menu, the menu key, and the Fill limit.
mods.notes: Better fix for the mouse cursor sticking in the middle of the screen on Linux: while the menu is open the game's own cursor-locking is skipped altogether, so the pointer is never snapped to the center. Plus a tip about the F menu, an AlwaysOpenMenu setting, smoother menu and Fill, and items listed lesser to greater. Feeds smelters, kilns, cooking racks, fires and fermenters from nearby chests.

mods.name: PartyHud
mods.description:
A party panel on the right of the screen showing every player in your world.

What it shows
- Each player's Steam picture, name, health, stamina and distance, live, at any range.
- F8 hides or shows the panel (handy for screenshots). It hides itself while menus are open.

Settings: how many players, size, opacity, position, and whether to show yourself, portraits and distance.
mods.notes: The panel hides while the inventory, crafting window, build menu, trader or big map is open. Tidier drawing (no leftover scale change). The F8 hide/show key works while holding Shift (running).

mods.name: QualityOfLife
mods.description:
Small controls that make the game nicer to play, each with its own switch.

What is in it
- Q: build a quick set from items you hover in your inventory; outside the inventory it swaps to the set and back.
- B: jump into construction mode with your hammer, and back to what you had.
- Stack to chests: a button under your inventory moves matching items into nearby chests, with Undo and sounds.
- K opens the chest assignment menu (choose what each chest receives); L locks items so they are never stacked.
Keys are configurable. Q and B work while you are running.
mods.notes: Better fix for the mouse cursor sticking in the middle of the screen on Linux: while the chest-assign menu is open the game's own cursor-locking is skipped altogether. Plus smoother menus, Stack to chests with Undo and sounds, chest assignment (K), item locking (L), and Q/B working while you run.

mods.name: Recycler
mods.description:
Build a Recycler with the hammer and turn old gear back into a share of the materials it was made from.

How it works
- Look at the Recycler and press E: pick a weapon, armor piece or tool from your inventory, see what it would return, and recycle it.
- You get about half of the materials back (50% by default; leftovers are a chance of one more). Recycler Presses built within 8 m raise this to 60% and then 75%.
- The gear must be one you could craft, and the crafting station it was made at (and its level) must be nearby. Equipped or upgraded gear asks for a second click. Items locked with L are skipped.
- Costs fine wood, iron and bronze. Restart the game after installing or updating it.

Settings: refund percentages, chance rounding, which gear types are allowed.
mods.notes: First version: a buildable Recycler with a crafting-station style menu, Recycler Press upgrades, chance-based rounding, station requirements, confirmation for valuable gear, sounds and synced spinning rollers.
mods.restart: It adds new build pieces. Restart the game after updating so they register cleanly.
